parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes to end the VAT exemption and business rates relief for private schools in order to invest the proceeds in state schools, and commits to protecting and improving school funding including recruiting additional teachers and providing free breakfast clubs in every primary school.

citations.quote: Labour will end the VAT exemption and business rates relief for private schools to invest in our state schools.
Labour will recruit an additional 6,500 new expert teachers.

results.headline: Labour pledges 6,500 new expert teachers in key subjects
results.quote: Labour will recruit an additional 6,500 new expert teachers.

results.headline: Labour MP challenges Conservatives on tuition fee legacy
results.quote: Given that plan 2 tuition fees were introduced by the Conservatives in 2012, that they froze the repayment thresholds in 2016 and that they abolished the maintenance grants, was that fair then?

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives commit to protecting day-to-day schools spending in real terms per pupil, building on record school funding levels, and propose funding 100,000 high-quality apprenticeships by curbing poor-quality university degrees.

citations.quote: School funding is at its highest ever level in real terms per pupil and there are record numbers of teachers, 27,000 more than 2010.
we will build on this progress in the next Parliament by protecting day-to-day schools spending in real terms per pupil.

results.headline: Conservatives claim children are best readers in the West
results.quote: We recruited record numbers of teachers to help our children become the best readers in the West.

results.headline: Conservative MP: Labour first introduced tuition fees
results.quote: I must be suffering from some sort of political amnesia, because I was absolutely convinced that it was a Labour Government that introduced tuition fees in the first place. Maybe the Minister will correct me.

results.headline: Conservative MP: Labour has now admitted student loans system is broken
results.quote: In January, the Chancellor was saying that the student loans system was 'fair and reasonable'. She now admits 'as of yesterday' that it is broken. In one sense, we have won this debate even before it started.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats pledge to increase school and college funding per pupil above the rate of inflation every year and to invest in clearing the backlog of crumbling school and college building repairs.

citations.quote: Increase school and college funding per pupil above the rate of inflation every year, and end the scandal of crumbling school and college buildings by investing in new buildings and clearing the backlog of repairs.

results.headline: Lib Dems pledge dedicated mental health professional in every school
results.quote: Putting a dedicated, qualified mental health professional in every school.
